operations.name: Blank Receiving Inspection
operations.setup_note: Receive the purchased annealed rings and verify material certification, condition, outside diameter, existing bore and axial width. Check that the specified machining allowance is available before releasing the blanks.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Lower Datum Side
operations.setup_note: Grip the upper blank OD in low-pressure bored jaws, exposing the lower face and internal profile; use the blank axis provisionally until the bore is machined. Establish datum B at the lower groove flank and finish the accessible lower OD band for reverse gripping.

operations.name: CNC Turn – Upper Side
operations.setup_note: Reverse into low-pressure soft jaws on the finished lower OD band, with a relieved axial locator contacting datum B without obstructing the upper bores. Face to finished overall width, complete the remaining OD band and machine the upper internal steps.

operations.name: In-Process Blank Inspection
operations.setup_note: Support the soft turned blank without distorting the ring and inspect the faces, stepped bores, relief and datum-B flank against the process axis. Release for shaping only after confirming tooth-tip pre-bore size, cutter clearance and available tooth-section geometry.

operations.name: Internal Gear Shaping – Rough and Finish
operations.setup_note: Locate the soft blank on datum B and center from the finished OD and tooth-tip pre-bore using a low-distortion ring fixture. Rough-shape then finish-shape the 70 internal teeth in one loading, establishing datum A at the gear pitch axis and producing the specified profile and crown.

operations.name: Tooth Chamfer and Deburr – Upper End
operations.setup_note: Support the shaped ring on datum B with the upper tooth ends exposed and center to datum A. Machine the upper tooth-end edge breaks and remove upper-side burrs while the ring remains soft.

operations.name: Tooth Chamfer and Deburr – Lower End
operations.setup_note: Reverse the ring in a protected fixture centered to datum A, exposing the lower tooth ends and transition at M. Complete the lower tooth chamfers and remaining general edge breaks, then confirm the ring is burr-free before carburizing.

operations.name: Continuous Carburize and Integral Quench
operations.setup_note: Load the soft, burr-free rings on distortion-control carriers through the in-house continuous carburizer with integral quench, targeting 1.2 mm effective case depth and 60–62 HRC after temper. Process the 100-piece order in qualified carrier loads rather than assuming one load; charge heat treatment per finished kilogram.

operations.name: Low-Temperature Temper
operations.setup_note: Transfer the quenched rings promptly to the qualified tempering cycle using supported carrier loads within equipment capacity. Temper to the customer-required final surface hardness of 60–62 HRC.

operations.name: Hardness and Effective Case-Depth Check
operations.setup_note: Check tempered surface hardness and verify 1.2 mm effective case depth using a representative witness coupon or approved metallurgical sample. Maintain traceability from the sample to the production carrier loads.

operations.name: Shot Blast – Quench Scale Removal
operations.setup_note: Support the hardened rings in qualified blast fixtures and remove quench scale without damaging the shaped tooth edges or datum flank. Split the order into equipment-rated loads; this is scale removal, not shot peening.

operations.name: Wash
operations.setup_note: Rack the hardened rings with the internal teeth and reliefs accessible to the wash flow. Remove blast media and residual contamination, then dry before inspection.

operations.name: Gear Inspection
operations.setup_note: Locate from datum B and evaluate the finished gear about datum A. Check tooth size over pins and perform sampled gear-analyser checks of profile, pitch, helix and load-side crown against the approved gear specification.

operations.name: Final Dimensional Inspection
operations.setup_note: Establish datum A from the gear pitch geometry and datum B from the lower relief flank without distorting the ring. Check final sizes and edge condition, with sampled CMM verification of the specified positional, profile and perpendicularity requirements after heat treatment.

operations.name: Identification Marking
operations.setup_note: Support the inspected hardened ring and apply identification at the approved optional marking location. Keep the mark clear of tooth working surfaces and datum-contact areas.

operations.name: Rust Preventive and Pack
operations.setup_note: Apply rust preventive to the clean, accepted rings and pack with separators protecting the internal teeth and datum surfaces. Preserve heat-treatment and inspection traceability for the 100-piece order.

clarifications.suggested_default: Use the component-table root diameter of 191.35–191.55 mm and reject the assumed 178.875 mm value.

assumptions.text: Linear dimensions are interpreted in millimetres, consistent with the routing-view dimensions and module specification.

Stock is a purchased annealed ring with 2.5 mm machining allowance per side: OD 208 + 5 = 213 mm, bore 181.026 − 5 = 176.026 mm, and axial width 53.8 + 5 = 58.8 mm. The 53.8 mm face width is the section A-A basic stack 16.5 + 37.3. The 13.11 mm dimension is Detail A only. No sawing, forging or drilling from solid is required. Finished weight is estimated at 2.796 kg: 16.5 mm at bore 188 mm, and 37.3 mm from OD 208 to root 191.45 plus 52.7 percent of the tooth annulus out to tip 181.026.

Feature descriptions establish datum A as the F01 gear pitch axis and datum B as the lower flank of F13. Before shaping establishes A, soft machining and blank inspection use a temporary process axis from the turned geometry; final datum relationships are verified after heat treatment.

The Ø181.026 tooth-tip envelope is cut by the gear shaper, not bored on the lathe. The component-table root range 191.35–191.55 mm provisionally overrides the geometrically inconsistent assumed root value.

Provisional access allocation places F04, F05 and F13 on the lower datum-side setup and F03 and F09 on the upper setup. The stepped lands are assumed not to overlap the active tooth span; section-layout clarifications must be resolved before machining.

F10 is interpreted as two axisymmetric end chamfers, one machined in each turning setup. F16 and F17 are allocated to the upper tooth end; F14, F18, F19 and F20 to the lower tooth end, subject to the complete drawing.
The R0.25 F06 blends are produced incidentally by the adjacent bore and taper finishing tools. F08 receives a dedicated internal form-grooving step because its R1.2 carries an explicit tolerance.

The gear shaper is assumed capable of producing the specified profile modification and 0.010–0.040 mm load-side crown using a qualified shaping process. Rough and finish shaping remain separate passes in one loading; neither tooth shaving nor tooth grinding is required.

Customer instruction requires in-house continuous carburizing with integral quench, followed immediately by tempering, to 60–62 HRC and 1.2 mm effective case depth. The 61 HRC entries represent the nominal midpoint, not a measured result; heat treatment is charged per finished kilogram.

The conditional 'Hard finish datums' template step is explicitly omitted under the BGL742-specific rule: no bore or face has a specified fit, Ra 0.8 or tighter, or size band below 0.05 mm. F13's 0.05 mm perpendicularity is not such a size band; all turned surfaces are finished soft and checked after heat treatment.

Hardness and case-depth verification use an approved representative witness coupon or metallurgical sample. Final CMM and gear-analyser checks are provisionally sampled, with the production sampling plan to be approved before release.

The external-gear sequence is inapplicable: this part has internal teeth, no off-axis holes or pockets, and requires neither hobbing nor a VMC setup. Deburring is completed before carburizing and is not repeated afterward.
